Zwitterionic Dissociation: Cationic (pH < pI) ⇋ Zwitterion (pH = pI, Net Charge = 0) ⇋ Anionic (pH > pI)
5.1 Isoelectric Point (pI) Mechanics & Electrophoretic Migration Behavior (pI = (pK_a1 + pK_a2)/2)
5.2 Chirality & Essential Amino Acids (PVT TIM HALL; Glycine is the Only Achiral Amino Acid)

quickSummary: Amino acids exist as dipolar Zwitterions carrying net zero charge at their Isoelectric Point (pI). At pH < pI, amino acids are cationic (migrate to cathode); at pH > pI, they are anionic (migrate to anode). All standard amino acids are chiral L-isomers EXCEPT Glycine (achiral). The 10 essential amino acids are PVT TIM HALL. Peptide bonds (-CO-NH-) have 40% partial double-bond character and are rigid and planar.
summary: Master amino acid zwitterion equilibria, isoelectric point calculations, electrophoretic migration, and peptide bond planarity.

summaryBox.title: Isoelectric Point & Electrophoresis
summaryBox.takeaway: At pH < pI: Cation (migrates to Cathode -). At pH > pI: Anion (migrates to Anode +). At pH = pI: Zwitterion with net charge = 0 (no migration).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
ZWITTERIONIC DISSOCIATION
                         
       H₃N⁺─CH(R)─COOH  ◄──[pH < pI]──  H₃N⁺─CH(R)─COO⁻  ──[pH > pI]──►  H₂N─CH(R)─COO⁻
        (Cationic Form)                   (ZWITTERION)                    (Anionic Form)

Isoelectric Point Formula: pI = [pKa1(COOH) + pKa2(NH3+)] / 2
• For Aspartic Acid (pKa1=1.88, pKa2=3.65, pKa3=9.60): pI = (1.88 + 3.65)/2 = 2.77.
conceptBreakdown.content: The Isoelectric Point ($	ext{pI}$) is the specific $	ext{pH}$ at which an amino acid carries a net electrical charge of zero and exists predominantly as a dipolar Zwitterion.

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PEPTIDE BOND PLANARITY
                           
                                  R₁       H   R₂
                                  │        │   │
                                ──C── C ── N ── C──
                                  │   ║   ║    │
                                  H   O   O    H
                                     [Peptide Bond]

• Glycine (H₂N-CH₂-COOH) is the ONLY achiral standard amino acid.
• 10 Essential Amino Acids (PVT TIM HALL): Phenylalanine, Valine, Threonine, Tryptophan, Isoleucine, Methionine, Histidine, Arginine, Leucine, Lysine.
• Peptide Bond (-CO-NH-) has ~40% partial double-bond character due to resonance, forcing rigid coplanar trans geometry.
conceptBreakdown.content: Peptide bonds are synthesized by dehydration condensation between the $lpha$-carboxyl and $lpha$-amino groups. Resonance delocalization creates a rigid planar unit preventing free rotation around the $	ext{C-N}$ bond.

quickRevision: At pH = pI, amino acid exists as Zwitterion (net charge = 0).
At pH < pI, cationic (migrates to Cathode -).
At pH > pI, anionic (migrates to Anode +).
Glycine is the only achiral standard amino acid.
All natural amino acids in proteins belong to L-series.
Essential amino acids mnemonic: PVT TIM HALL.
Peptide bond has 40% double-bond character (rigid planar trans).
